title: Pocket and the Tiny Light
markdown:
The sun dipped low and painted the sky in rose and lavender, the most peaceful colours of the day. In a room that felt wonderfully large and full of playful echoes, Velvetmane the unicorn nestled close to Pocket the mouse. Velvetmane's coat was the colour of a wispy cloud, and her mane shimmered like a stream in moonlight. Pocket was a tiny creature with whiskers that could sense the whisper of a dandelion fluff. As the day began to fade, the room, which usually felt so cozy, began to seem just a little too wide. The corners deepened, holding secrets that made Pocket's little heart flutter like a moth in a gentle breeze. The tall bookshelves seemed to lean in. The space between Pocket's little mouse-sized bed and the grand soft rug felt wider than ever before, a pale sea of carpet with no island but the unicorn's hoof.

Pocket, nestled close to Velvetmane's warm velvety leg, let out a tiny sigh, a puff of air so small it barely disturbed the soft fur. His brave whiskers, usually so perky and full of curiosity, drooped ever so slightly, like the petals of a sleepy flower.

"It's so… wide, Velvetmane," he whispered, his voice barely a breath against the quiet hum of the coming night. He imagined himself, just a tiny speck, lost in all that quiet space.

Velvetmane, who loved Pocket dearly and always tried to make him feel safe and grand, no matter how small he felt, lowered her noble head, luminous eyes filled with gentle concern. She nuzzled his small furry ear, the touch as soft as a falling feather.

"I know, little friend," she murmured, her voice a low melodious rumble, like the softest lullaby sung by the wind through willow trees. "Sometimes even the coziest places can feel a bit too big when the light starts to fade and the world outside grows dim. I wish I had something to make it feel more snug, a place where worries can't tiptoe in."

It was then, as Velvetmane pondered their quiet wish for more coziness, that she remembered. Tucked away on a high shelf, nestled among a pile of soft moss that smelled faintly of damp earth and fallen leaves that whispered secrets of autumn, was a tiny stubby candle. It was no bigger than Pocket's paw, and its wick, a little grey twist, was almost hidden by the waxy white of the candle itself.

"Wait here, my dear Pocket," Velvetmane said softly, her voice laced with a hopeful whisper.

With a gentle inclination of her head she reached, ever so carefully, for the little candle. She had to stretch. The shelf was high even for a unicorn who was used to being tall. Dust, as fine as flour, drifted down and landed on Pocket's whiskers. He sneezed a mouse sneeze, polite and small. Velvetmane did not hurry. She brought the candle down as if it were a sleeping bird.

Pocket peered at it, bright eyes wide. It seemed so small, so very small indeed, especially in their now-shadowy room.

"Can this little thing help?" he wondered aloud, his voice tinged with a hopeful tremor, like a tiny bell on a distant breeze.

Velvetmane nodded, her silvery mane shimmering with a soft glow of its own. "Let us see," she whispered, her belief in even the smallest things a comfort in itself.

With a delicate practised flick of her magic horn, a tiny soft flame sprang to life on the wick. It was a small flame, no bigger than a firefly's wink, and it cast a warm gentle glow that seemed to sway with the quietest breath, a shy little dancer in the deepening twilight.

And oh, what a wondrous difference it made.

The tiny candle's soft light did not chase away all the shadows, for shadows are just quiet resting places for the light. But it made them seem friendly, like sleepy quiet helpers nestled in the corners, no longer deep and mysterious. The vast room no longer felt so wide and lonely. The gentle flicker danced upon the walls, making them feel closer, warmer, as if they were drawing a soft knitted blanket around them, a hug of light. The bookshelves stopped leaning. They became only shelves again, full of stories that could wait until morning. The rug shrank back into being a rug, not a sea. Pocket's little bed, which had looked like a leaf on a pond, looked like a bed.

Pocket snuggled deeper into Velvetmane's side, feeling the gentle rise and fall of her breathing, his whiskers twitching with pure contentment. He watched the flame. It bowed when Velvetmane breathed. It stood up again, stubborn as a daisy. Wax smelled faintly of the mossy shelf, of autumn leaves and a little honey. Pocket stretched one paw toward the glow, not quite touching, and felt the warmth as if the candle had noticed him on purpose. The little flame, so small and unassuming, made their cozy corner feel like the safest warmest most welcoming place in the whole wide world.

Velvetmane kept her horn still, so the flame would not startle. A floorboard ticked, then thought better of it. Outside, a last bird made a small remark and went to bed. Pocket's whiskers, which had drooped, stood up again, perky as morning, though morning was hours away.

Soon, feeling safe and wonderfully snug, tucked close together with the little candle casting its warm friendly glow, Velvetmane and Pocket drifted off to sleep. They dreamed of gentle lights and quiet wonders. The flame kept its small post. The rose-and-lavender sky outside finished fading. Inside, the room was the right size at last, and the candle — no bigger than a paw — went on being enough.
